scope: Independent review of the working-tree diff against the requested base, untracked foundation implementation, and relevant inherited controller, release/push gates, standalone installer, OS-isolation harness, owner tests and three protected workflows. Revised schema-1 foundation scope: no trusted-runtime automatic deployment, no new mappings, Jump DENY, existing v2.2.1 approvals retained.

logic_errors.finding: The protected v2 CI contracts job deterministically fails on these candidate bytes. Only the release-gate version assertion was updated. The controller assertion still requires 2026.09.08-hermes-autopilot.2 and the push-gate assertion still requires 2026.09.08-dvizh-git-push-gate.1; both sources now report 2026.09.11 versions ending .2.3.2. With set -Eeuo pipefail, the first mismatch aborts contracts and prevents its dependent release-gate job from succeeding.
logic_errors.evidence: T4 independently executed all three exact grep commands extracted from the workflow in OS isolation: controller exit 1, release exit 0, push gate exit 1. The 156-test suite nevertheless passed; its new version test checks only dvizhrelease. This is an actual implementation/workflow mismatch, not a missing owner pin prerequisite.
logic_errors.required_resolution: Coordinate all three version contracts with the reviewed candidate and validate the actual protected workflow static step before issuing an approved base. No fixes made in this review.

logic_errors.finding: Foundation readiness is reported as successful without checking its mandatory owner authorization. Release doctor checks tool availability and pending state only; push doctor checks key/transport authorization only. Neither validates owner-approval.json. The controller aggregates these ok fields, so its documented mandatory readiness check can be green while every production push/release fails because the foundation approval is absent or invalid.
logic_errors.evidence: T4 ran the actual release doctor function with only root requirement/tool availability/pending-state probes substituted, and an owner_manifest spy configured to reject missing authorization. doctor returned ok=true and never invoked the spy. Push doctor and controller aggregation were inspected statically; no key, transport or production doctor was accessed. Authorization paths still fail closed: this is a readiness/delivery diagnostic defect, not an authorization bypass.
logic_errors.required_resolution: Expose and validate foundation authorization readiness through the doctor contract, distinguish unavailable/invalid owner trust from transport readiness, and make aggregate readiness reflect the prerequisites. The owner must still provide the authorization independently.

suggestions.suggestion: Exercise the complete version/static workflow contract instead of checking one version string. A green unit suite did not detect L1.

Keep the inherited v2.1 installer smoke explicitly labeled as legacy coverage. It does not validate privileged installation of this v2.3.2 bootstrap/installer. Preserve the documented owner-side staging, interpreter, manifest, identity and transport validation prerequisites; do not count legacy smoke as current delivery acceptance.

The eventual owner rollout should explicitly align the controller's managed-job base branch with the independently approved foundation base, as well as the workflow variable and both gates' manifest. No base, ref or pin was changed during review.

boundary_assessment.caller_git: Implemented privilege-separated caller Git: explicit invoking UID/primary GID cross-check, extra_groups=[], fixed cwd '/', constructed environment, absolute Git binary, explicit hook/fsmonitor/helper/transport overrides. Caller repository config/includes are still parsed, but in the caller-identity subprocess rather than root. Actual privileged identity transition was not executed; subprocess arguments are covered by T1.
boundary_assessment.immutable_push: Implemented private temporary bare repository without copied config/hooks/refs/alternates/shallow files, opaque pack export, strict index-pack, captured commit existence, ancestry/count/merge checks, per-commit scope validation and external base/head pins. Push refspec uses captured SHA. T1/T4 exercise real export and adversarial mutations; transport is spied/mocked, never pushed. No authorization bypass demonstrated in this review.
boundary_assessment.ci_and_history: External fixed-path manifest is implemented in both gates and is not derived from candidate assertions. Required five paths include all three protected workflows and both validators. Release walks every single-parent commit, comparing protected leaf changes, and requires exact successful CI run/job identities. Push rechecks every commit after export. Tests reject pinned substitutions and hidden protected history. L1 remains a functional protected-workflow failure.
boundary_assessment.bootstrap: Standalone buffered launcher and bootstrap are delivered. External digests authenticate bootstrap then installer before execution; isolated/no-site interpreter and standalone standard-library installer remove adjacent candidate imports. Installer digests and installs captured buffers with trusted staging metadata and transaction handling. T1/T5 confirm buffer replacement behavior. No authenticated owner channel or actual root installation was exercised.
boundary_assessment.release_scope: Schema 2 rejected. Only the existing three static targets can be automatic. Former runtime-auto targets require existing approval; three privileged targets retain exact source/SHA/metadata/full-phrase policy. Manual/shared frontend/server remain approval-required. Jump target/restart denial retained. No new runtime behavior-test obligation imposed.
boundary_assessment.functional_entrypoints: Unconditional root quarantine removed and fixed production configuration accepted by entry checks. Real privileged entrypoints were not run. Readiness contract is incomplete (L2); this must not be described as unconditional quarantine.
boundary_assessment.resource_and_platform_limits: Timeouts and compressed export file-size limit exist. Exhaustive hostile-object resource exhaustion, simultaneous independent gate invocations, OS/Git vulnerabilities, power-loss durability and every possible race are not proven safe by these bounded fixtures.
